title: Warmup actor sequencing labbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal labbook for sequencing warmup actors and cohort rollout for model flips / pin transitions. This is a working list — lots of open questions, rough timing, and telemetry hooks. Use as a checklist during the next staged release window.

High-level goal:
- Ramp new model variant without causing client-visible latency regressions or quality regressions.
- Prime caches/kv so first requests in a cohort don't pay cold KV cost or misaligned quantization path costs.
- Ensure per-tenant pin/unpin works and falls back safely.

Definitions I'm using:
- Actor: an automated job or traffic type used to "prime" the serving stack (e.g., synthetic priming requests, shadowed client requests, SDK-driven warm calls).
- Cohort: group of users/tenants defined by fraction, region, product SKU, or traffic channel.
- Pin: sticky binding of a tenant to a model version for a TTL.

Warmup sequencing proposal (ordered steps):
1) Silent priming (no metric exposure) — internal-only synthetic traffic from warmup runner.
   - purpose: populate KV caches, warm CUDA kernels, lazy-load model quant tables.
   - runner config: 5 qps to each replica for 3 minutes, sequences length distribution matching production 0-512 tokens.
   - watch: GPU mem, load spikes, OOMs.

2) Shadow priming — send real production requests to the variant in shadow mode (responses discarded).
   - purpose: exercise model paths with live input distribution (edge cases).
   - target: 0.5–1% of production qps, distributed across regions. Duration 10–20m.
   - watch: latency p95 delta vs baseline shadow path; any errors returned by variant (decoding, tokenization mismatches).

3) Mini-cohort (internal beta customers + low-impact tenants) — 0.5% traffic for 15–30m.
   - include both SDK and direct API clients.
   - enable per-tenant pin for cohort with 1h TTL.
   - collect quality signals (LLM-eval short tests, agreement with golden prompts).

4) Expand cohort in steps (0.5 -> 2 -> 5 -> 20 -> 50) with 30–60m cool-off between steps depending on signals.

Per-step checklist (to run before increasing fraction):
- Telemetry baseline established for previous step.
- Error budget used < 20% of allocated for this step.
- Latency SLO: p95 increase < 80ms vs baseline for each region.
- Cost regression: per-token GPU time increase < 10% (informal check).
- Quality regression: rolling eval mismatch < 1.5% (configurable).
- Rollback button verified (SDK toggle + console route) and person on-call ready.

Pinning notes and heuristics:
- Use sticky pin TTLs to avoid immediate flip-flopping for SDK clients. Default: 1 hour for beta cohorts, 6 hours for broader cohorts, 24 hours for full rollout unless forced unpin required.
- Pin ownership: SDK-serverside should honor tenant pin then fallback to route-level default. Document mismatch cases with SDK versions older than v0.9.
- Unpin on detected regression: set TTL to 0 and throttle traffic away for the tenant, then queue for manual follow-up.

Priming strategies by actor type:
- Synthetic priming: low-cost, predictable; won't catch tokenization edgecases. Use for kernel warm and KV population only.
- Shadow priming: catches distribution issues but adds cluster load; route to idle capacity or burst pool.
- Client-driven priming (SDK warm calls): most realistic, but requires coordination with client teams for rate limits and cost.

Telemetry + guardrails (must-have signals):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 broken down by route/model/region.
- Errors: decoder exceptions, tokenization errors, grpc/codes != 0, 5xx spikes.
- Quality: automated short eval suite (10–30 prompts) per cohort run every 10m; embed-based similarity vs golden baseline for semantic drift.
- Cost: tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batch sizes.
- Recovery: daily snapshot of KV cache hit ratio after priming to measure effectiveness.

Automations I want to test during warmups:
- Auto-throttle shadow qps when p95 delta > 60ms for two consecutive windows.
- Auto-fast-fail cohort expansion if error rate > threshold.
- Automatic TTL reduction for pinned tenants if backend signals mismatch (eg: model not compatible) — but only as a soft corrective, not full rollback.

Rollforward / rollback runbook (quick):
- Immediate rollback (hot): flip SDK override to previous model id, set tenant pin TTL=0, drain variant via routing layer (2min target). Notify release channel.
- Gradual rollback: reduce cohort fraction by half every 10m until back to 0. Monitor quality signals and escalate if needed.
- Postmortem checklist: collect traces, last 1h of token-level latency, top 10 failing tenant ids, golden eval diffs.

Open questions / risks I keep seeing:
- How to account for client-level caching that hides priming benefit? We might be priming but client caches prevent cold calls reaching the server for X minutes.
- Cost of shadowing at scale: need to validate ready burst capacity for large numbers. Must coordinate with infra for capacity hedging (reserved burst nodes).
- Pin TTL semantics for multi-region clients — sticky pin may prefer one region's model variant leading to cross-region inconsistency.

Ad-hoc notes / quick todos:
- Talk to infra SRE (Ravi) about pre-reserving 4 n1-standard-burst replicas in us-west for 2 hours during the expansion window.
- Add an integration test in the serving-runtime repo that simulates 100 synthetic priming requests and verifies KV hit rate improves > 70%. (PR linked above).
- Ask DX (Maya) to surface a small "warmup" flag in SDK to opt-in for priming requests from clients for internal beta tenants.
- Add a short prompt set (30 prompts) to the eval suite specifically covering tokenization edgecases and copy-paste heavy inputs.

Final thought for the next run: schedule a short 20m dry-run the day before with the release-team to exercise the rollback path (manual first, then automated). Mark the dry-run as required in the preflight checklist.

-- E.T.
